messages:
maya: Hey — seeing intermittent 401s from our .NET client when running in CI. Works locally. headers we set: `Authorization: Basic <redacted>`
maya: Example snippet: `client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("API_KEY"))));`
alex: quick check — are you sure the env var doesn't include a trailing newline or CRLF? CI secrets sometimes include an extra newline from copy/paste.
maya: hmm could be. I printed length locally and it looked fine. How do I reliably check base64 value in CI?
sam: you can print the raw base64. e.g. in linux runner: `echo -n "$API_KEY:" | base64` (note the -n). For node: `console.log(Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64'))`. That shows what header should be.
alex: also important: basic auth encodes `username:password`. If API expects the key as username with empty password you must b64(api_key + ':'). If they expect it as the password with empty username then b64(':' + api_key). Know the server's expectation.
maya: our server docs said "use Basic with your key as the password and empty username" — so it should be `':' + key`. I might have used the other form locally by accident and the CI secret is slightly different.
sam: PowerShell gotchas: `echo`/`Write-Output` adds CRLF. For pure base64 in pwsh use: `[Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes(":$env:API_KEY"))` — that avoids newline.
maya: ah, good call. Our CI runs on Windows hosted runner sometimes. I'll add that snippet to the job to verify.
alex: Another small thing: some shells treat quotes differently. In GitHub Actions you might see the secret with surrounding quotes if someone included them when creating the secret. Try `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | od -An -t x1` to spot stray characters.
maya: ran `printf` in the CI job — saw `0d` bytes (CR). So the secret had a CR. Removing the CR fixed it. thanks.
dev-bot: deploy-checklist: remembered to rotate the invalid key? :robot_face:
maya: yep rotated and pushed a tiny CI job to assert `echo -n` bytes count > 16 so we catch tiny trailing-chars.
sam: FYI Node/axios example for reference: `const encoded = Buffer.from(process.env.API_KEY + ':').toString('base64'); axios.defaults.headers.common['Authorization'] = `Basic ${encoded}`;`
alex: and curl check quick one-liner: `curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n ":$API_KEY" | base64)" https://api.example.test/health`
maya: added short note in the repo README about which side (username vs password) to use and included the pwsh/posix snippets.
sam: nice, that'll save others. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all, closing this thread."
